what: Distribution strategy: current npm ships readable JS + bash scripts. To protect source code, compile to binary via `bun compile`. MCP server + CLI becomes single binary, hooks become thin bash wrappers calling the binary. Distribute via homebrew/curl/npm-wrapping-binary. Same TypeScript codebase, just different build target. Pro features with server-side logic are the only truly unbypassable protection. Local pro flags can always be edited. Also: window-style recall pagination (offset/limit/exclude_ids) and search dedup independence from recall — both as fast follows.
why: User realized npm freeware exposes all source code. Wants path to closed-source distribution while maintaining easy install. Binary compilation is easiest path.
